How a Moving Block Enters the Twice-Contracted Fourth Derivative

Source: R/outer_refresh.R
trace_refresh4.Rd

The part of \(\mathrm{tr}(M\,U[v,u])\) that trace_design_form does not compute, where \(U\) is the second derivative of \(K\) in the coefficients contracted in two directions.

Usage

trace_refresh4(spec, M, params, Hl, dv, du, units)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec.

M

The matrix the trace is taken against.

params

The parameter names.

Hl

The link-scale curvature, from refresh_hessian.

dv, du

The two directions, from refresh_direction.

units

The refreshable terms, from refresh_units.

Value

A single number.

Details

Differentiating the three contributions of \(\partial K/\partial\beta\) once more leaves three further terms that read \(\partial X/\partial\beta\) and one that would read \(\partial^2X/\partial\beta^2\). Writing \(D_a = (\partial X_a/\partial\beta)v\) and \(E_a = (\partial X_a/\partial\beta)u\), $$N = N_1 + N_2 + N_3, \qquad N_1[(a,j),(b,k)] = -\sum_i w_i\Big(\sum_m \ell_{abm}(X_mv_m)_i\Big) E_a[i,j]X_b[i,k],$$ \(N_2\) the same with the two directions exchanged, and \(N_3[(a,j),(b,k)] = -\sum_i w_i\ell_{ab,i}D_a[i,j]E_b[i,k]\), which is supported where BOTH blocks move. The correction is \(\mathrm{tr}(M(N + N^\top)) = 2\sum M\odot N\), and the first two pieces are read off refresh_amat with the third derivative in place of the curvature, so neither \(N\) nor any contraction is assembled.

The omitted term carries \(\partial^2X/\partial\beta^2\), the term's own third derivative, which no contract supplies. Measured on a bilinear \(f\), where it is exactly zero, the corrected Hessian reaches the reference's own floor.

See also

trace_design_form, contract3_refresh
